entities.summary:
Benedetto da Maiano was an Italian sculptor of the Early Renaissance period, born in Florence, Italy, around 1440, and died on June 2, 1497, in Florence.

He was a prominent artist of his time, known for his exquisite marble sculptures, particularly his portraits and decorative reliefs. Maiano's style was influenced by the classical Greek and Roman art, which was a hallmark of the Renaissance humanist movement.

Maiano's most famous works include the altarpiece for the Cathedral of Florence and the decorative sculptures for the Palazzo Vecchio. His art not only showcased his technical skill but also his deep understanding of human anatomy and emotion.

Maiano's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a significant role in the development of the Renaissance art movement in Italy and beyond.

"The soul of Florence is in Benedetto da Maiano," said his contemporary, the artist Andrea del Verrocchio."
